\section[fe]{\fa{ف} (fe) — the letter that opens \fa{فکر}}

\label{lesson:FA-W26-fe}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: write \fa{ط} and \fa{ظ} once each, and name them.

Now say \textbf{\fa{فکر} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{fekr kardan}), \textquotedblleft{}to think\textquotedblright{}. You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one letter out of it and puts it in your hand.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script you'll notice: \fa{ف}}
\textbf{\fa{ف}} — \emph{fe}, the sound \emph{f}.

It opens \textbf{\fa{فکر}} (\emph{fekr}), \textquotedblleft{}thought\textquotedblright{}, in \textbf{\fa{فکر} \fa{کردن}}. A small closed \textbf{head} on a broad bowl, with \textbf{one dot above}.

\subsection*{Writing: \fa{ف}}
\hlblockfigure{\detokenize{figures/FA-W26-fe-filmstrip.pdf}}{How \fa{ف} is written, stroke by stroke}

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textbf{1.} start here: loop clockwise around the small closed head
  \item \textbf{2.} continue left through the broad bowl without lifting
  \item \textbf{3.} lift once, then place the upper dot last — and only now lift
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Pen lifts: 1.}

\begin{quote}
Stroke order is one attested teaching order; hands and teachers vary. Source: Persian Online, How to Write Persian Characters, \fa{ف} demonstration at 02:09–02:13 (Liberal Arts Instructional Technology Services, Univ. of Texas at Austin).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Look:} at \textbf{\fa{فکر} \fa{کردن}} and point at \fa{ف} inside it
  \item \emph{Trace it:} \fa{ف} three times, saying \emph{f} as you finish each one
  \item \emph{Write it:} \fa{ظ}, then \fa{ف}, from memory
  \item \emph{Read it:} \textbf{\fa{فکر} \fa{کردن}} aloud once more
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which letter is this — \fa{ف}? (\textbf{fe}, \emph{f}.) Which word did it come from? (\textbf{\fa{فکر} \fa{کردن}}, \emph{fekr kardan}, \textquotedblleft{}to think\textquotedblright{}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ghâf]{\fa{ق} (ghâf) — the letter inside \fa{خوشوقتم}}

\label{lesson:FA-W26-ghaf}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: write \fa{ظ} and \fa{ف} once each, and name them.

Now say \textbf{\fa{خوشوقتم}} (\emph{khoshvaghtam}), \textquotedblleft{}pleased to meet you\textquotedblright{}. You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one letter out of it and puts it in your hand.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script you'll notice: \fa{ق}}
\textbf{\fa{ق}} — \emph{ghâf}, a \emph{gh} made far back in the throat.

It is inside \textbf{\fa{خوشوقتم}} (\emph{khoshvaghtam}), \textquotedblleft{}pleased to meet you\textquotedblright{}. Its head is the head of \textbf{\fa{ف}}, from the last lesson, but it carries \textbf{two dots}, and standing alone its bowl dips below the line.

\subsection*{Writing: \fa{ق}}
\hlblockfigure{\detokenize{figures/FA-W26-ghaf-filmstrip.pdf}}{How \fa{ق} is written, stroke by stroke}

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textbf{1.} start here: loop counterclockwise around the small closed head
  \item \textbf{2.} continue down and left through the deep bowl without lifting
  \item \textbf{3.} lift once, then place the upper-right dot
  \item \textbf{4.} lift again, then place the upper-left dot — and only now lift
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Pen lifts: 2.}

\begin{quote}
Stroke order is one attested teaching order; hands and teachers vary. Source: Persian Online, How to Write Persian Characters, \fa{ق} demonstration at 02:14–02:18 (Liberal Arts Instructional Technology Services, Univ. of Texas at Austin).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Look:} at \textbf{\fa{خوشوقتم}} and point at \fa{ق} inside it
  \item \emph{Trace it:} \fa{ق} three times, saying \emph{gh} as you finish each one
  \item \emph{Write it:} \fa{ف}, then \fa{ق}, from memory
  \item \emph{Read it:} \textbf{\fa{خوشوقتم}} aloud once more
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which letter is this — \fa{ق}? (\textbf{ghâf}, \emph{gh}.) Which word did it come from? (\textbf{\fa{خوشوقتم}}, \emph{khoshvaghtam}, \textquotedblleft{}pleased to meet you\textquotedblright{}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[alef-e madd]{\fa{آ} (alef-e madd) — the alef that opens \fa{آمدن}}

\label{lesson:FA-W26-alef-madd}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: write \fa{ف} and \fa{ق} once each, and name them.

Now say \textbf{\fa{آمدن}} (\emph{âmadan}), \textquotedblleft{}to come\textquotedblright{}. You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one letter out of it and puts it in your hand.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script you'll notice: \fa{آ}}
\textbf{\fa{آ}} — \emph{alef} with a \textbf{madd}, the long \emph{â} at the start of a word.

It opens \textbf{\fa{آمدن}} (\emph{âmadan}), \textquotedblleft{}to come\textquotedblright{}. It is \textbf{\fa{ا}}, which you already write, wearing a small wavy \textbf{hat}. A plain \textbf{\fa{ا}} at the start of a word says a short \emph{a}; the hat makes it a long \emph{â}.

\subsection*{Writing: \fa{آ}}
Put your pen on \fa{آ} and follow its line. Copy the shape you can see — slowly, and larger than it is printed.

\begin{quote}
This book does not yet tell you \textbf{where to start this letter or which way to travel}. It is not written down here until it can be written down with a source. Copying what is in front of you needs no such source, and it is how the shape gets into your hand in the meantime.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Look:} at \textbf{\fa{آمدن}} and point at \fa{آ} inside it
  \item \emph{Trace it:} \fa{آ} three times, saying \emph{â} as you finish each one
  \item \emph{Write it:} \fa{ق}, then \fa{آ}, from memory
  \item \emph{Read it:} \textbf{\fa{آمدن}} aloud once more
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which letter is this — \fa{آ}? (\textbf{alef-e madd}, \emph{â}.) Which word did it come from? (\textbf{\fa{آمدن}}, \emph{âmadan}, \textquotedblleft{}to come\textquotedblright{}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
